questions.stem: Suppose it is proposed that all university students should be required to learn academic writing. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
It has recently been proposed that all university students should be required to learn academic writing. In my view, this proposal deserves our full support, for such a skill is far more than an optional refinement.

For one thing, academic writing trains students to organize ideas logically and cite sources honestly. When I wrote my first term paper, I struggled to structure arguments and nearly copied online material by mistake; a writing course would have taught me both clear reasoning and academic integrity. For another, this ability pays off well beyond campus. Whether a graduate applies for a research position or drafts a report at work, the capacity to express thoughts precisely on paper often determines success.

Admittedly, mastering academic writing takes time and effort. Nevertheless, the long-term rewards clearly outweigh the cost. Therefore, I strongly believe universities should make this course compulsory, ideally starting from the first year so that students benefit throughout their studies.

transcript.text: Customs and Border Protection officials are seeing a rise in people illegally bringing eggs from Mexico into border states, such as Texas.
transcript.zh: 美国海关与边境保护局官员发现,从墨西哥非法携带鸡蛋进入得克萨斯州等边境州的人数正在增加。

transcript.text: The U.S. average price for a dozen large eggs last month hit $4.25. That's more than double their $1.78 price in December, 2023. Meanwhile, 30 eggs in Mexico sell for just $3.4.
transcript.zh: 上个月美国一打大号鸡蛋的平均价格达到4.25美元。这是2023年12月1.78美元价格的两倍多。与此同时,墨西哥30个鸡蛋的售价仅为3.4美元。

transcript.text: Those bringing eggs into the U.S. risk fines of up to $10,000. But officials say they usually seize and destroy the eggs. They also impose a $300 penalty. The Department of Agriculture banned eggs from Mexico in 2012. This was due to the risk of bird flu. Officials said most people arriving at international borders with eggs are truthful about their purchases. They simply don't know bringing eggs is not allowed.
transcript.zh: 将鸡蛋带入美国的人面临最高1万美元的罚款。但官员表示,他们通常会没收并销毁鸡蛋。他们还会处以300美元的罚金。农业部于2012年禁止从墨西哥进口鸡蛋。这是由于禽流感的风险。官员表示,大多数携带鸡蛋抵达国际边境的人对其购买行为如实申报。他们只是不知道携带鸡蛋是不被允许的。

transcript.text: "Generally, the items are declared during the first inspection. Then the person can abandon the eggs without consequence," a Customs and Border Protection spokesperson said.
transcript.zh: 美国海关与边境保护局发言人表示:"通常情况下,这些物品在首次检查时就会申报。然后当事人可以放弃这些鸡蛋而不会产生后果。"

transcript.text: Even so, there have been a very small number of cases recently when authorities discovered eggs during further inspections.
transcript.zh: 即便如此,最近仍有极少数情况是当局在进一步检查时发现了鸡蛋。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the egg price in the U.S.?

options.text: It has risen because of bird flu.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The U.S. average price for a dozen large eggs last month hit $4.25. That's more than double their $1.78 price in December, 2023.信号：数字对比+more than double 。答案句的信号是数字加比较：hit $4.25 与 more than double their $1.78 price——从 1.78 涨到 4.25、还『翻了不止一倍』…

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：It has been fluctuating. 说价格『来回波动』，但录音只给了从 1.78 到 4.25 的单向上涨，没有任何下跌或反复，方向不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It has risen because of bird flu. 把上涨原因归给禽流感。录音确实念到 bird flu，但那是解释 The Department of Agriculture banned eggs from Mexico（为何禁止从墨西哥带蛋）的原因，不是涨价的原因——盗用了原词却接错了因果。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：It has been consumers' concern. 说蛋价成了消费者的担忧。录音通篇没提消费者的态度或担忧，只客观报了价格数字，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（more than double their $1.78 price ↔ gone up sharply 倍数=大幅）

questions.evidenceText: The U.S. average price for a dozen large eggs last month hit $4.25. That's more than double their $1.78 price in December, 2023.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about most people arriving at American borders with eggs?

options.text: They don't want to abandon their eggs.
They don't know they will be heavily fined.
They don't know they are forbidden to bring eggs.
They don't declare their eggs during the inspection.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Officials said most people arriving at international borders with eggs are truthful about their purchases. They simply don't know bringing eggs is not allowed.信号：题干同词组+紧跟解释句 。答案句信号是题干原词组在录音里复现：most people arriving at international borders with eggs 几乎照搬了题干，它后面紧跟的 They s…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：They don't want to abandon their eggs. 说他们不愿放弃鸡蛋。录音里确有 abandon the eggs 这个词，但原文是说『在第一次检查时申报、然后可以无后果地放弃鸡蛋』，根本没说他们『不愿放弃』——盗用 abandon 一词，意思却恰相反。 借用原文：Those bringing eggs into the U.S. risk fines of up to $10,000.
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：They don't know they will be heavily fined. 说他们不知会被重罚。录音里 risk fines of up to $10,000、a $300 penalty 确实提到罚款，但原文说这群人不知道的是『带蛋被禁止』，不是『不知会被罚款』——把『不知禁令』偷换成了『不知罚款』。 借用原文：Generally, the items are declared during the first inspection.
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：They don't declare their eggs during the inspection. 说他们检查时不申报。录音里 declared during the first inspection 确实有 declare 和 inspection，但原文是说『物品一般会在第一次检查时被申报』，即多数人是申报的，与选项的『不申报』正好相反。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（They simply don't know bringing eggs is not allowed ↔ They don't know they are forbidden to bring eggs. not allowed=forbidden）

questions.evidenceText: Officials said most people arriving at international borders with eggs are truthful about their purchases. They simply don't know bringing eggs is not allowed.

transcript.text: Nettie's House, a restaurant in America, has been hit with criticism after announcing on the website that children under the age of 10 are no longer welcome.
transcript.zh: 美国一家名为Nettie's House的餐厅在其网站上宣布不再欢迎10岁以下儿童后遭到批评。

transcript.text: Among the reasons given for the decision, the restaurant cited "noise levels, lack of space for high chairs, cleaning up crazy messes, and the liability of kids running around the restaurant". They decided that it was time to take control. The decision wasn't made lightly, but some recent events pushed them to implement this new policy.
transcript.zh: 餐厅给出的决定理由包括"噪音水平、高脚椅空间不足、清理混乱不堪的场面以及孩子在餐厅跑来跑去的责任问题"。他们决定是时候采取管控措施了。这个决定并非轻率做出,但最近发生的一些事件促使他们实施这项新政策。

transcript.text: Responding to the post, one person commented that "It is messed up beyond another level. Children are children. Mums are tired and don't have time to cook. Not welcoming children under 10 is a complete slap in the face to families." He felt so disappointed in the establishment.
transcript.zh: 针对这篇帖子,有人评论说"这简直乱得不成样子。孩子就是孩子。妈妈们很累,没有时间做饭。不欢迎10岁以下儿童完全是对家庭的一记耳光。"他对这家餐厅感到非常失望。

transcript.text: There are others, however, who showed support for the restaurant's decision. They said it has the right to implement any rules it wants.
transcript.zh: 然而,也有其他人对餐厅的决定表示支持。他们说餐厅有权实施任何它想要的规定。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about the restaurant Nettie's House?

options.text: It is no longer critical of younger customers.
It has banned kids under 10 from dining there.
It is no longer as noisy and crowded as before.
It has implemented a decision to expand business.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Nettie's House, a restaurant in America, has been hit with criticism after announcing on the website that children under the age of 10 are no longer welcome.信号：新闻首句点题，机构名后紧跟核心事件 。短篇新闻第一句通常就把核心事件说清。这里店名之后紧跟 announcing on the website that children under the age of 10 ar…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：It is no longer critical of younger customers. 借了原文"针对低龄顾客"这层意思，却说餐厅"不再挑剔年轻顾客"——恰恰相反，餐厅是收紧了对儿童的限制；而且 no longer critical 的是公众对餐厅的批评，不是餐厅对顾客的态度，方向反了。 借用原文：noise levels
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It is no longer as noisy and crowded as before. 抓住了原文提到的 noise levels（吵闹）来勾人，但原文只是把吵闹列为出台新规的"理由"，从没说餐厅现在已经变得不吵不挤了。听到 noise 就选 C 就中了原词陷阱。 借用原文：implement this new policy
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：It has implemented a decision to expand business. 蹭了原文里 implement this new policy 的 implement 一词，但原文实施的是"谢绝儿童"的新政策，根本没提扩张生意，expand business 是无中生有。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（children under the age of 10 are no longer welcome ↔ banned kids under 10 from dining there "不再欢迎"="禁止用餐"的同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: Nettie's House, a restaurant in America, has been hit with criticism after announcing on the website that children under the age of 10 are no longer welcome.

questions.stem: What do supporters say in response to the restaurant's new policy?

options.text: It is fully aware of frequent customers' feelings.
It caters to the tastes of different customers.
It is entitled to adopt any rules it wants.
It should announce its decisions online.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P4）：There are others, however, who showed support for the restaurant's decision. They said it has the right to implement any rules it wants.信号：转折 however 引出支持方，应答句紧随 。第4段以 There are others, however, who showed support 用转折词 however 把镜头从前文反对者切到支持者，紧接着 T…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：It is fully aware of frequent customers' feelings. 说餐厅"充分了解常客的感受"，但支持者原话只讲"餐厅有权定规矩"，从没提常客（frequent customers）也没说店家了解谁的感受，这层意思原文整个没出现。
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：It caters to the tastes of different customers. 蹭了全篇反复出现的 customers 一词，但支持者说的是"店家有权定规矩"，不是说它"迎合不同顾客的口味"——caters to tastes 在原文没有依据，是借熟词编的好听话。 借用原文：announcing on the website
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：It should announce its decisions online. 蹭了原文 announcing on the website 的"网上宣布"，但那只是叙述餐厅当初怎么发的公告，支持者根本没说"店家应该在网上公布决定"，且 should 是建议口吻、与本题问的支持表态不符。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（it has the right to implement any rules it wants ↔ It is entitled to adopt any rules it wants has the right=is entitled，implement=adopt）

questions.evidenceText: There are others, however, who showed support for the restaurant's decision. They said it has the right to implement any rules it wants.

transcript.text: Security officers were searching a suburb in Australia where an adult snake was believed to be wandering after the discovery of a huge, "freshly shed" snake skin.
transcript.zh: 在澳大利亚一个郊区发现了一张巨大的"新脱落"蛇皮后,安全官员正在搜寻该地区,据信有一条成年蛇在游荡。

transcript.text: The skin was found at a construction site, and the government wrote to residents to warn them. They were told to observe and, if possible, photograph the animal. If it was moving, watch where it went. It was recommended not to make contact with the animal.
transcript.zh: 这张蛇皮是在一处建筑工地发现的,政府向居民发出书面警告。他们被告知要观察这条蛇,如有可能对其拍照。如果它在移动,要观察它去了哪里。建议不要与该动物接触。

transcript.text: The type of snake was determined to be one of the world's largest snake species. It is not poisonous, but can still attack and kill its victims. This type of snake is classified as a threat to humans, especially small children, as well as pets. They may carry viruses that are fatal to native snakes, which do not have resistance.
transcript.zh: 经确定,这种蛇是世界上最大的蛇类物种之一。它没有毒性,但仍然可以攻击并杀死猎物。这种蛇被归类为对人类构成威胁,特别是对幼儿以及宠物。它们可能携带对本地蛇类致命的病毒,而本地蛇类对这些病毒没有抵抗力。

transcript.text: If officers found the snake, they would employ a licensed snake catcher to catch it and transport it to a specialist animal doctor, the government said. If caught, the snake would be examined to determine where it came from, how long it had been in the area, what it had been eating, whether it was carrying any diseases of concern and whether it had produced babies.
transcript.zh: 政府表示,如果官员找到这条蛇,他们将雇用有执照的捕蛇人将其捕获并运送到专业动物医生处。如果被捕获,将对这条蛇进行检查,以确定它来自哪里、在该地区待了多长时间、吃了什么、是否携带任何令人担忧的疾病以及是否产下了幼蛇。

questions.stem: What does the report say security officers were searching for?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Security officers were searching a suburb in Australia where an adult snake was believed to be wandering after the discovery of a huge, "freshly shed" snake skin.信号：搜寻主语句直接点对象 。答案句是新闻第一句，把『谁在搜+搜什么』一并说清：an adult snake was believed to be wandering（一条成年蛇据信在游荡），这才是被搜寻的活物；蛇皮 sn…

optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了录音里真实出现的 a huge, "freshly shed" snake skin（巨大的刚蜕的蛇皮），听到 huge 和 skin 很想选 A huge animal skin.。但蛇皮只是引发搜寻的线索，搜寻的对象是活蛇本身，故 C 答非所问。 借用原文：a specialist animal doctor
optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：录音通篇说的是一条野生大蛇，从未提到这是谁走失的宠物。A missing pet. 在原文中没有依据，属凭常识臆测（『蛇会不会是谁养的跑了』），录音没说就不能选。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：A snake specialist.（捕蛇/治蛇专家）盗用了录音后文 a licensed snake catcher 与 a specialist animal doctor 的概念，但这些人是抓到蛇之后才会请的，不是此刻搜寻的对象。把『搜寻蛇』偷换成『搜寻专家』，张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（an adult snake ↔ A grown-up snake. adult=grown-up 同义改写）

questions.evidenceText: Security officers were searching a suburb in Australia where an adult snake was believed to be wandering after the discovery of a huge, "freshly shed" snake skin.

questions.stem: Where does the report say the discovery was made?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The skin was found at a construction site, and the government wrote to residents to warn them.信号：地点状语 at 直接给地点 。答案句里 The skin was found at a construction site 的 at a construction site 是典型的地点状语，正面回答了『发现在哪』。…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项盗用了同句里的 the government 一词，听到 government 就想选 In a government office.。但录音里政府是『写信提醒居民』的施动方，并非发现蛇皮的地点，二者无关，属答非所问。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：In a deserted house.（废弃房屋）录音从未提到，可能是考生凭『蛇出没=破旧荒地』的常识脑补出来的。原文只说工地，没说废屋，无依据。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：At a local zoo.（本地动物园）也是常识联想（『蛇=动物=动物园』），录音里完全没有出现 zoo。原文发现地是工地，不是动物园，排除。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（found at a construction site ↔ At a construction site. 地点词原样对应）

questions.evidenceText: The skin was found at a construction site, and the government wrote to residents to warn them.

questions.stem: What did the government say would be done if security officers found what they were searching for?

options.text: Figuring out where it came from.
Curing it of any possible diseases.
Determining how to catch it safely.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：If caught, the snake would be examined to determine where it came from, how long it had been in the area, what it had been eating, whether it was carrying any diseases of concern and whether it had produced babies.信号：If caught 引出后续措施 。答案句以 If caught（一旦抓获）开头，正对题干的 if…found 假设条件，后面 would be examined to determine where it came…

optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：选项盗用了录音 whether it was carrying any diseases of concern 里的 diseases 一词，听到『病』就想选 Curing it of any possible diseases.。但原文只是『检查它是否携带疾病』，并非『治好它的病』，把『检查』偷换成『治疗』，故错。 借用原文：whether it had produced babies
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：选项盗用了 whether it had produced babies 里的 babies，让人误选 Protecting its babies against harm.。但原文是『查清它是否产过幼蛇』，根本不是『保护幼蛇不受伤害』，方向完全不同，属偷换概念。 借用原文：employ a licensed snake catcher to catch it
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：Determining how to catch it safely. 盗用了 catch（抓）。录音里抓蛇是 employ a licensed snake catcher to catch it（雇持证捕蛇人去抓），是直接安排人去抓，并不是『研究怎样安全地抓』，故 D 答非所问。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（examined to determine where it came from ↔ Figuring out where it came from. determine=figure out 同义）

questions.evidenceText: If caught, the snake would be examined to determine where it came from, how long it had been in the area, what it had been eating, whether it was carrying any diseases of concern and whether it had produced babies.

transcript.text: W: Poor Hannah!
transcript.zh: W: 可怜的Hannah!

transcript.text: M: Why? What happened?
transcript.zh: M: 怎么了?发生什么事了?

transcript.text: W: Didn't you hear? She won a TV competition and became a millionaire overnight.
transcript.zh: W: 你没听说吗?她赢了一个电视竞赛,一夜之间成了百万富翁。

transcript.text: M: No way. That's incredible. Are you kidding?
transcript.zh: M: 不会吧。太不可思议了。你在开玩笑吗?

transcript.text: W: No, I'm serious. I swear it. She went on a TV show where they quiz on general knowledge, and she won first prize.
transcript.zh: W: 没有,我是认真的。我发誓。她参加了一个电视节目,那种考常识问答的,然后她赢得了头奖。

transcript.text: M: Wow. That's so lucky of her. How much did she win?
transcript.zh: M: 哇。她太幸运了。她赢了多少钱?

transcript.text: W: I'm not sure of the exact figure, but it's a few million Euros, maybe five million Euros after tax.
transcript.zh: W: 我不确定具体数字,但有几百万欧元,税后大概五百万欧元。

transcript.text: M: I can't believe it. You're really not joking, are you?
transcript.zh: M: 我真不敢相信。你真的不是在开玩笑,对吧?

transcript.text: W: Honestly, look at my face. Our friend Hannah won a ton of money.
transcript.zh: W: 真的,你看我的表情。咱们的朋友Hannah赢了一大笔钱。

transcript.text: M: Unbelievable. Then why were you saying "poor Hannah"?
transcript.zh: M: 难以置信。那你为什么说"可怜的Hannah"?

transcript.text: W: Well, it turns out that she's spent it all already.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯,结果她已经把钱全花光了。

transcript.text: M: Five million Euros? How is that even possible?
transcript.zh: M: 五百万欧元?这怎么可能?

transcript.text: W: She bought a house for herself and her husband, a house for her parents, and then a house for each of her four brothers and sisters. And then she bought her husband a ridiculously expensive sports car.
transcript.zh: W: 她给自己和丈夫买了一套房子,给她父母买了一套房子,然后又给她四个兄弟姐妹每人买了一套房子。之后她又给她丈夫买了一辆贵得离谱的跑车。

transcript.text: M: Wow. Are they all happy? Because that's what matters, isn't it?
transcript.zh: M: 哇。他们都开心吗?因为这才是最重要的,不是吗?

transcript.text: W: I know for a fact Hannah isn't. You see, she was planning to quit the job she hates and retire early. But now that she ran out of money, she can't. Basically, she miscalculated how fast she was burning through the money, and she's now full of regret.
transcript.zh: W: 我确定Hannah不开心。你看,她本来计划辞掉她讨厌的工作,提前退休。但现在她钱花光了,做不到了。基本上,她错误估计了花钱的速度,现在她满心懊悔。

transcript.text: M: Why don't they sell that flashy new car?
transcript.zh: M: 他们为什么不把那辆炫酷的新车卖掉?

transcript.text: W: She wants to, but her husband refuses to get rid of it. He says the car is the best thing that has ever happened to him, and if she sells it, he will divorce her.

transcript.text: Analytical decision-making is a decision-making approach where a manager makes important business decisions only with solid data. This style contrasts with more instinctive leadership styles where managers make many decisions using instinct or opinion. While analytical decision-makers benefit from a deliberate, thoughtful approach, this style also has some shortcomings.
transcript.zh: 分析型决策是一种决策方法,管理者仅凭可靠数据做出重要商业决策。这种风格与更依赖直觉的领导风格形成对比,后者的管理者运用本能或观点做出许多决策。虽然分析型决策者受益于审慎、深思的方法,但这种风格也存在一些缺陷。

transcript.text: A key flaw with analytical decision-making is that it takes time. While this approach is beneficial when you have the time and the decision is important, it is problematic when time is crucial. Analytical decision-makers struggle with deadlines and a sense of urgency with decisions. In situations where you need more timely action, decisions based on some information and instinct may work better.
transcript.zh: 分析型决策的一个关键缺陷是耗费时间。虽然当你有时间且决策重要时这种方法是有益的,但当时间紧迫时就会产生问题。分析型决策者难以应对截止日期和决策的紧迫感。在需要更及时行动的情况下,基于部分信息和直觉的决策可能效果更好。

transcript.text: The desire to be right is a major driver of analytical decision-making. Leaders who use this style don't want to make mistakes. This commitment, one right way of thinking or doing things, hinders the manager's flexibility. Inflexibility causes you to ignore or avoid listening to the thoughts and ideas of others. You only want to utilize hard data or facts.
transcript.zh: 追求正确是分析型决策的主要驱动力。采用这种风格的领导者不想犯错。这种对唯一正确思维或做事方式的执着,妨碍了管理者的灵活性。缺乏灵活性导致你忽视或避免倾听他人的想法和观点。你只想利用硬数据或事实。

transcript.text: Despite its restrictions, analytical decision-making does have several key strengths. By relying on facts and data, you minimize your potential for a wrong decision. You also get away from the habit of making guesses or following instincts. Database technology enables business leaders to look to hard evidence in analyzing target markets and promotional strategies, rather than making assumptions or guesses on what works.
transcript.zh: 尽管存在局限性,分析型决策确实具有几个关键优势。通过依赖事实和数据,你将做出错误决策的可能性降至最低。你也摆脱了猜测或遵循直觉的习惯。数据库技术使商业领导者能够依靠确凿证据来分析目标市场和促销策略,而不是对有效方法进行假设或猜测。

transcript.text: Branyas was born in the United States on April 4th, 1907. But her family moved to Spain, where they were originally from, when she was a young child. She has lived there ever since.
transcript.zh: Branyas于1907年4月4日出生在美国。但她的家人在她还是小孩时搬回了他们原来所在的西班牙。从那以后她就一直住在那里。

transcript.text: The 115-year-old is active on social media, regularly sharing aspects of her life. She also shares some of her secrets to living so long. These include playing the piano from a young age. Unfortunately, she had to give up the practice seven years ago at 108.
transcript.zh: 这位115岁的老人活跃在社交媒体上,经常分享她生活的方方面面。她还分享了一些长寿的秘诀。其中包括从小弹钢琴。不幸的是,她在七年前108岁时不得不放弃了这个练习。

transcript.text: Her other secrets for living a long life? She led an active lifestyle until her later years, but has never followed a specific diet. "Many people ask me what diet I follow to live so many years," Branyas wrote. "I have always eaten little, but everything, and I have never followed any plan." But she does eat yogurt every day, which she said has "an infinite number of positive properties" for the body. She has also said that the secret to a long life is "knowing how to choose" what to forget.
transcript.zh: 她长寿的其他秘诀?她在晚年之前保持着积极的生活方式,但从未遵循过特定的饮食。"很多人问我遵循什么饮食才能活这么多年,"Branyas写道。"我一直吃得很少,但什么都吃,从未遵循过任何计划。"但她确实每天吃酸奶,她说酸奶对身体有"无数积极的作用"。她还说过长寿的秘诀是"知道如何选择"要忘记什么。

transcript.text: "Life would be impossible if we remembered everything," she said.
transcript.zh: "如果我们记住一切,生活将是不可能的,"她说。

transcript.text: It's the first day of school, and your teacher tells you to find a seat in the classroom. Where do you sit? Does it matter? Yes. It does matter where you sit in your classroom, so choose and choose carefully. Studies report that where you sit in the classroom can impact your ability to learn and the way your teacher perceives you. Guess what else? Your grade.
transcript.zh: 这是开学第一天,老师让你在教室里找个座位。你会坐在哪里?这重要吗?是的。你坐在教室的哪个位置确实很重要,所以要慎重选择。研究表明,你在教室里的座位会影响你的学习能力以及老师对你的看法。你猜还有什么?你的成绩。

transcript.text: Then what is the best seat in the classroom?
transcript.zh: 那么教室里最好的座位是哪里呢?

transcript.text: In one study, students who sat in the front and center of the classroom received a higher grade average and scored higher on tests than those sitting towards the back of the classroom. Get this. Students sitting in the middle of the classroom also outscored students sitting behind them. This study gathered that students had a clearer vision of the blackboard and were able to focus more attention on the instructor. By sitting front and center, students were able to hear better too.
transcript.zh: 在一项研究中,坐在教室前排和中间位置的学生比坐在教室后排的学生获得了更高的平均成绩,考试分数也更高。还有一点。坐在教室中间的学生的成绩也超过了坐在他们后面的学生。这项研究发现,学生们对黑板有更清晰的视野,能够将更多注意力集中在授课教师身上。坐在前排和中间位置,学生们也能听得更清楚。

transcript.text: The instructors said that they also formed a better connection with the students who sat in front. Perhaps the connection is made because of eye contact and visibility and more interaction. But when you sit in the front row, you may be called on more by your teacher, mainly due to the fact that you are easier to see. So for students who are not prepared and for those who are extremely shy, the attention could cause some unwanted stress.
transcript.zh: 授课教师表示,他们与坐在前排的学生建立了更好的联系。也许这种联系是由于眼神交流、可见度以及更多互动而形成的。但是当你坐在前排时,你可能会更多地被老师提问,主要是因为老师更容易看到你。所以对于没有准备好的学生以及极度害羞的学生来说,这种关注可能会带来一些不必要的压力。

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The gaming industry is larger than films and music combined, yet few of us are likely to list our achievements in playing computer games as work experience in our résumé. But why not? Businesses are waking up to the skills gamers can bring to the workplace.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: One start-up is convinced that the skills learned by playing games — hard-won through years of training and battle — can be applied to real-life work situations. And Game Academy reckons its belief is backed up by hard data. Do you enjoy unusual puzzle games like Portal, or tower defence games like Defense Grid? The team has found that IT workers play those more than average. But if you prefer Civilization, Total War, or X-Com, where strategy and resource management are key, then you might have more in common with managers.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Game Academy's idea is simple: analyse gamers' habits from their online gaming profile, and offer courses in valuable skills that reflect their aptitudes — skills they can practise and refine in-game. And there is already a growing acceptance that gaming skills are transferable.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Even the military is hiring gamers. "The ability to absorb information, react swiftly and coordinate actions whilst remaining calm under pressure are often attributes of people that are good at gaming," according to a Royal Air Force spokesperson. Those skills are part of what the Royal Air Force is looking for "in a variety of roles". "Skills acquired through gaming can be very relevant to certain areas."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "There are plenty of soft skills that gamers can utilise in a professional setting, such as teamwork, problem solving and strategic planning," says Ryan Gardner, a regional director with Hays recruitment. But does that really mean your top 100 ranking in Overwatch should go down in your résumé? "It's about how you either make it relevant to the job you are applying for, or how it makes you more interesting as a potential employee," Mr Gardner says.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Two years ago, a Glasgow University study made headlines for suggesting gaming could make students more successful. But "the research hasn't really changed minds, at least not yet," says one of the authors of the study, Dr Matthew Barr. He's now writing a book on the topic. "For now, I think the negative reputation around games means that telling someone you're a determined gamer is more likely to harm your chances of getting a job. But if someone can explain how they've led a team in an online game, for example, they may be able to persuade an employer that this is useful," says Dr Barr.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Playing games casually is unlikely to help your career prospects. But part of Game Academy's suggestion is to transform casual gamers into "conscious" ones, applying critical thinking to developing their skills. "We see gameplay as a resource of talent," says co-founder David Barrie. "Why can't we put in our résumé our gaming victories and achievements?" he asks. "If they say they want leadership — why can't I point to my years of leading World of Warcraft raids?"

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: There are already plenty of gamers out there who know that their hobby has made them who they are. Earlier this year, Matthew Ricci told gaming site Kotaku: "If you're playing EVE Online you basically already have an MBA." Often made fun of in gaming circles as a "spreadsheet simulator(电子表格模拟)", the economy of the fictional EVE universe is driven by real market principles. If you want to build a new spaceship, the raw material has to be mined by another player. Manufacturing costs come into effect, and commodities fluctuate in price based on demand and the distance to haul the commodity.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Mr Ricci, who had always dreamed of being the boss of his own company, ran an in-game corporation comprising hundreds of players. Eventually, he realised he could transfer his skills to real-life business — instead of doing it for free. He restructured Zentech, once a taxation vehicle for his father's business, and it is now in its fourth year helping international brands enter the Canadian market. EVE teaches skills like creativity, leadership, organisation, and conflict resolution, he maintains. He credits his success to his family, his strong desire to run his own business — and "a damn good company in Iceland that made a damn good game".

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Digital entrepreneur and business consultant Mia Bennett says: "In more traditional settings, gaming is still imagined to be the pursuit of teenage boys — a waste of time." But there are some links to skills like "decision-making, the ability to anticipate and future planning," she says. "It also helps with meta-skills — learning how to learn, experimentation, and creative thinking."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Twelve years into his career, Mark Long, a radiotherapy physicist with the NHS in Surrey, doesn't get as much gaming time as he used to. "I would love to say that my gaming skills allow me to destroy cancer using linear accelerators like photon(光子) blasters, but that's not quite the reality." Instead, he credits old-school games like Palace of Magic with exposing him to computers. Every new gaming upgrade improved his knowledge of how they worked. Gaming also encouraged a competitive spirit — and that, he believes, translates. "When creating treatment plans, the aim is to optimise the radiation dose to the tumour and restrict it as much as possible to healthy surrounding tissues and organs," he says. It's about "repeating the process, but each time doing something slightly different to improve the result". Not unlike achieving a high score or a perfect run. "Most videogames are essentially puzzles to solve," he says. "And problem-solving is a big part of my job."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: "Over at Game Academy, Mr Barrie is aware they still have a mountain to climb. The employer community will need the science," he says, but confesses he only became a true believer when he started asking players about their biggest in-game achievements. "The scale and scope of their answers were amazing," he says. "But ask them the same about their work, and they don't know." "The engagement and powerful skills that people get playing a game — why can't work be like that?" he asks.
